data.chip: A fully discrete R-2R resistor ladder with a separate discrete native DSD decoder. No part number: the ladder is the converter.

device_settings.why: The device has a user-selectable non-oversampling mode, set from the front panel or the remote. The maker's own mode list, from the user manual: « The 2nd and 3rd digit from the left on bottom: OS and NOS mode select. While working under oversampling (OS) mode, the lower the oversampling level is, the warmer the sound will be. While working under non-oversampling (NOS) mode , the sound even more warmer and smoother. The possible values are: N0 : New NOS mode. N1 : Classis NOS mode. O2 : 2X oversampling O4 : 4X oversampling O8 : 8X oversampling » - « Classis » is the page's spelling. Selecting N0 or N1 takes the interpolation filter out of the path, which is the precondition `correctable` requires.

data.chip: A fully discrete R-2R resistor ladder with a separate discrete native DSD decoder. No part number: the ladder is the converter.

device_settings.why: The device has a user-selectable non-oversampling mode, set from the front panel or the remote. The maker's own mode list, from the user manual: « The 2nd and 3rd digit from the left on bottom: OS and NOS mode select. While working under oversampling (OS) mode, the lower the oversampling level is, the warmer the sound will be. While working under non-oversampling (NOS) mode , the sound even more warmer and smoother. The possible values are: N0 : New NOS mode. N1 : Classis NOS mode. O2 : 2X oversampling O4 : 4X oversampling O8 : 8X oversampling » - « Classis » is the page's spelling. Selecting N0 or N1 takes the interpolation filter out of the path, which is the precondition `correctable` requires.

data.chip: « 8 group built-in 24bit R-2R decoders and 4 native DSD decoders work with balanced mode », on DA-7 modules. Note the ladder's own depth: 24 bit, while the inputs accept 32.

device_settings.why: There is NO OS/NOS selector in this model's manual, and the maker says why: it « only built in the optimize NOS mode ». So non-oversampling is not a setting here, it is the device. Same state as the MHDT Labs range and the LampizatOr Pacific 5, reached a third way: not by having no filter to begin with, but by a maker deleting the oversampling its own sibling offers.

data.chip: A fully discrete R-2R resistor ladder with a separate discrete native DSD decoder. No part number: the ladder is the converter.

device_settings.why: The device has a user-selectable non-oversampling mode, set from the front panel or the remote. The maker's own mode list, from the user manual: « The 2nd and 3rd digit from the left on bottom: OS and NOS mode select. While working under oversampling (OS) mode, the lower the oversampling level is, the warmer the sound will be. While working under non-oversampling (NOS) mode , the sound even more warmer and smoother. The possible values are: N0 : New NOS mode. N1 : Classis NOS mode. O2 : 2X oversampling O4 : 4X oversampling O8 : 8X oversampling » - « Classis » is the page's spelling. Selecting N0 or N1 takes the interpolation filter out of the path, which is the precondition `correctable` requires.

data.chip: A fully discrete R-2R resistor ladder with a separate discrete native DSD decoder. No part number: the ladder is the converter.

device_settings.why: The device has a user-selectable non-oversampling mode, set from the front panel or the remote. The maker's own mode list, from the user manual: « The 2nd and 3rd digit from the left on bottom: OS and NOS mode select. While working under oversampling (OS) mode, the lower the oversampling level is, the warmer the sound will be. While working under non-oversampling (NOS) mode , the sound even more warmer and smoother. The possible values are: N0 : New NOS mode. N1 : Classis NOS mode. O2 : 2X oversampling O4 : 4X oversampling O8 : 8X oversampling » - « Classis » is the page's spelling. Selecting N0 or N1 takes the interpolation filter out of the path, which is the precondition `correctable` requires.

The maker's own mode list, from the user manual: « The 2nd and 3rd digit from the left on bottom: OS and NOS mode select. While working under oversampling (OS) mode, the lower the oversampling level is, the warmer the sound will be. While working under non-oversampling (NOS) mode , the sound even more warmer and smoother. The possible values are: N0 : New NOS mode. N1 : Classis NOS mode. O2 : 2X oversampling O4 : 4X oversampling O8 : 8X oversampling » - « Classis » is the page's spelling. Selecting N0 or N1 takes the interpolation filter out of the path, which is the precondition `correctable` requires.

data._why_the_series_3_is_an_edition_and_not_: The maker's own page carries the Series 3 text inside the 3P page and says the Series 3 « can be fully upgraded to an Alpha DAC Reference Series 3P ». Two names, one upgradable object, and no fact on the page distinguishes them: that is the definition of `edition` here, not of `neighbour`. If a fact ever separates them - a rate, a filter, a converter - the edition becomes a record of its own.

data.chip: « Dual ESS ES9028Q2M DACs », from the page's own « DIGITAL TO ANALOGUE CONVERTERS » row.

device_settings.why: « Selectable, Fast - Slow - Short delay » - three filters, NAMED, in a specification row. The third is the one to prefer: a short-delay (minimum-phase) response puts the filter's ringing energy after the impulse rather than before it, and pre-ringing is the artefact apodising filters exist to remove - the same reasoning as Rockna's « hybrid phase ». The names are the ES9028Q2M's own filter menu exposed to the user, which is the first time in this catalogue a maker has done that instead of hiding it.

data.chip: TWO conversion sections in one box: « ein TDA1307 und zwei TDA1547 Chips » - Philips parts from the 1990s - and « 8 x ESS9039SPRO ». The maker calls them « Classic » and « Modern » and lets the owner choose between them.

device_settings.why: « Classic » runs the TDA1547 section, « Modern » the eight ESS9039SPRO, and an « Auto Mode » table switches by rate - « 96 / 192 / 384 / 768 kHz -> Modern ». Modern is the setting because it is the only one the maker's own table associates with high rates, and because the Classic section is built on parts rated for 16-bit material. A listener choosing Classic is choosing a sound, deliberately, and this catalogue has no business arguing with that - but Auto cannot plan around a converter it cannot identify.

data.chip: No part number, and none to expect: « four precision R-2R converter networks per channel, with all resistors mounted on a common silicon substrate » - eight networks in a dual-mono device, built rather than bought. The substrate is the notable part: a monolithic resistor array is how a ladder's matching is held, and the maker volunteers it.

source.quote: CH Precision's own page for the C1.2 DAC, read 2026-11-24. On the conversion stage: « the fully differential, dual-mono DAC architecture employs four precision R-2R converter networks per channel, with all resistors mounted on a common silicon substrate ». On the filter: « The C1.2's proprietary PEtER Spline Upsampling Filter has been further refined to operate at 32-bit fixed-point precision » and « By prioritizing time-domain coherence and minimizing pre- and post-ringing artifacts, the Spline Filter preserves transient integrity ». On the inputs: « Standard digital inputs include CH-Link HD, AES/EBU, S/PDIF, and Toslink, while optional boards enable high-resolution network streaming over Ethernet and asynchronous USB playback. »; « The C1.2 can be fitted with an optional Ethernet Streaming HD input board »; « For computer-based audio, the dedicated USB_IN board supports USB input. »; « The optional CLOCK_SYNC board adds a clock input and two outputs on high-quality BNC connectors »; « The third slot may also be configured with an additional Digital HD input board if required. »; « high-resolution PCM and DSD delivered over Ethernet or USB »; « Through the proprietary CH-Link HD connection, the D1.5 Transport delivers native DSD and MQA data directly to the C1.2 ». Self-description: « The C1.2 DAC marks a new chapter in CH Precision's approach to digital playback » and « The C1.2 is more than a next-generation DAC. »

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.

open_doubt.a_contradiction_to_settle: This doubt says the internal_bypass threshold is the QUTEST's, read from that model's manual. But the claim's internal_bypass carries its OWN source, the brand-level forum sentence above. One of the two is wrong, and it matters because this doubt also says the bypass rate is the figure to check first, since it is the one that changes an answer. Not acted on: measured and written down.
open_doubt.device_level_outcome: KEPT, after checking each field against this record's own quote rather than by analogy with the per-input withdrawal. The quote reads « passing 705.6/768k PCM to a Chord DAC bypasses the built-in WTA1 stage » - it names the rate AND it names the subject at brand level, which is exactly what this catch-all is. So pcm_max_hz: 768000 is supported here, unlike iFi's and MSB's, and `dsd_max` was already "unknown". Removing it for symmetry with the other records would have thrown away a fact its evidence carries.
evidence_kept: Chord Qutest user manual, read 2026-11-20: USB type B 32-bit/768 kHz PCM and up to DSD512; two BNC coaxial at 24-bit/384 kHz, reaching 768 kHz only in the dual-data mode that pairs with the maker's own upscaler; optical 24-bit/192 kHz, DSD64.

SENTENCE WORTH KEEPING, and the reason this is written down rather than deleted: several retailer listings give the Qutest's optical input as 96 kHz, where the manual says 192. Whoever opens a per-model Qutest record will meet that contradiction again, and this is where the answer already is - the manual was the figure taken.
open_doubt.resolution: The per-input ceilings were WITHDRAWN on 2026-11-24. This record's `model` is "unknown" - it is the brand's catch-all, standing for the Qutest, the Hugo, the Dave and the Mojo at once - and per-input ceilings cannot be true of all of them. The claim's own source said whose they were: the Qutest user manual. Keeping them meant asserting one model's inputs for four devices, which is the over-reach this doubt already named.
open_doubt.text: This is the brand's catch-all, and its per-input ceilings and its internal_bypass threshold are the QUTEST's, read from that model's manual. They are asserted here for the Hugo, the Dave and the Mojo as well, on evidence that names only one of them - the same over-reach the iFi record writes down. The rate at which the WTA1 stage steps aside is the figure to check first, since it is the one that changes an answer.
open_doubt.what_remains_unsupported: native_dsd: false and dop: true are not in the quote. They are not an over-reach but an instance of this import batch's known defect - one citation for ten facts - and they belong to the per-field evidence work, not to this withdrawal.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: A per-model record (chord/qutest) carrying these ceilings with this same manual as its source. The figures are not wrong; the subject they were attached to was.

data.chip: No converter chip, by design: « Chord Electronics custom coded Xilinx Artix 7 (XC7A15T) FPGA » driving a « 10 element pulse array design ». The FPGA runs the filter - « Tap-length: 49,152 » - and the pulse array does the conversion.

device_settings.why: Four filters, NAMED, in a user-options block: « Incisive neutral (Ultimate reference) (White) », « Incisive neutral HF roll-off (Green) », « Warm ('Smooth') (Orange) », « Warmer HF roll-off (Red) ». The first is the one to prefer and the maker says why in its own label - « Ultimate reference ». The other three are deliberate departures: two roll off the high frequencies, two are voiced « warm ». Auto's job is to deliver the signal intact and let nothing colour it, so the reference filter is the setting.

data.chip: No converter chip: « Xilinx Artix 7 FPGA, custom-coded by Chord Electronics' Rob Watts » with « 86x 208MHz cores running in parallel », running « advanced 16FS WTA 1 filter with 98,304-taps » into « a 10-element design » pulse array. Twice the tap length of the Hugo 2's 49,152.

device_settings.why: « four-stage user-selectable filter controls » - a count and no names, on a page that gives the tap length to five significant figures. The Hugo 2's page names its four; this one does not. No value can be recorded, and the Hugo 2's names must NOT be copied across: two models of one maker with the same filter COUNT is not evidence that the filters are the same.

open_doubt.text: Chord publishes TWO different ceilings for this device's optical input: 96 kHz on the product page (stated twice, in the spec table and in the Key Features list) and 192 kHz in the Qutest User manual 2.1. Both claims are recorded. The build resolves by source weight, which puts the page (datasheet, 70) above the manual (65) and therefore lands on the conservative 96 - defensible, and not the same as knowing. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the device itself. An optical input is the one ceiling a probe establishes for free, and this is a clean example of why level 2 is worth collecting even where a maker has published something.

data._why_the_da2_is_a_neighbour_and_not_an_e: The page is explicit that they are different products: « The DA2i builds on the DA2's strengths with noticeable improvements in resolution, timing, and control. » A customer testimonial on the same page writes « The DA2i / DA2 V3 », which suggests the DA2 reached a third revision. Facts DO distinguish them - the maker says so - and the DA2 has no record here, so the name resolves to this one for want of its own. That is `neighbour`, the relation that says « a DIFFERENT product, resolved here ». No figure on this record may be read as the DA2's.
data.chip: No part number, and none exists: « Next generation 16xDSD proprietary discrete dual differential D-to-A converters (MDAC2) », « in-house DACs », « proprietary Dual Differential DACs ». The maker states the stage's own rate - « our flagship 16xDSD (DSD1024) converter » - and that is the rate it RUNS AT, not the rate it accepts. « a newly designed Class A analog output stage » is the analogue stage. MDAT2 is the DSP ahead of the converters, MFAST the frequency acquisition, MCLK3 the clock.

open_doubt.text: Whether this device reconverts incoming PCM to DSD, and at what rate. The shape is unmistakable and the page will not say it. The converters are « 16xDSD » and « MDAT2 DSP works in harmony with the 16xDSD DACs, processing audio in real-time » - a discrete stage that runs at DSD1024 with a DSP in front of it, fed inputs that top out at 24/192 PCM and DSD128. Something upstream must be taking 192 kHz PCM to DSD1024, and pcm_reconverted_to_dsd would be the field for it. The page never states it. Nagra says it in one sentence (« Every input signal is converted into DSD 256 format ») and APL HiFi in another (« All PCM rates from the digital sources are converted to DSD, prior to D/A conversion »), both recorded today; this maker, whose founder built the first DSD systems, says only that its DSP works « in harmony with » the DACs. No fact is written. The inference is strong, which is the reason to be careful rather than a reason to proceed.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: The DA2i brochure or manual, both linked from the product page and neither read. Failing that, one sentence from EMM Labs. Do NOT resolve it from the sister MA3i page, which carries the same bullets and says no more, nor from the architecture: a 16xDSD stage is evidence of what the stage does, not of what happens to the signal before it.

data.chip: DUAL MONO: an AK4191 modulator with an AK4499 converter PER CHANNEL, as the maker's table says twice - « Left Channel: AK4191+AK4499 », « Right Channel: AK4191+AK4499 ». Four AKM parts in two roles. The third record in this catalogue on the AK4191+AK4499 pairing, after gustard/a26 and eversolo/dmp-a8, and the clearest argument yet that a chip model needs a role AND a count per part: « AKM » says nothing about whether a modulator is shared or doubled.

open_doubt.text: `kind` CANNOT SAY WHAT THIS DEVICE IS. It is filed as network_player, in the maker's own words - the page heads it « DMP Streamer Series - DMP-A8 » - and it is equally a USB DAC: the same table lists a USB-B Audio INPUT taking DSD512 and 768 kHz 32-bit from a computer. The field holds one value out of dac and network_player, and this device is both. This is the FIRST record of the population pass and it broke the field immediately, which is worth more than the record: the installed base is full of streamers with a DAC inside and a USB input on the back, and they will all land on this. Picking one value quietly would hide it. Either `kind` becomes a list, or it is renamed to say what it actually answers - how the device is REACHED - and a separate field says whether it converts.

open_doubt.text: How many selectable digital filters does this device have? Ferrum's own two pages give four different answers: « two included at launch », « three filter settings », « four digital filters created for Ferrum by Signalyst », and « One is a part of the ESS DAC, and four were designed especially for WANDLA ». The readings are not even consistent in kind - some count ESS's, some Signalyst's, some both. It matters because selectable filters are a level-3 fact: which one is active changes what the device does to the signal, and a consumer that upsamples needs to know whether its own work will be filtered again. One email to Ferrum settles it.

data.chip: CS43198 (Cirrus Logic), with an SA9312L as USB receiver and an MS8422N for S/PDIF - this page is unusual in naming the S/PDIF receiver separately from the USB one.

device_settings.why: « Supports 8 filter settings » - a count and not one name. No value can be recorded: the setting exists, the eight options are not published, and the ES9039Q2M's own filter menu is a chip feature the maker has not described. It is the second maker in this catalogue to state a filter COUNT and withhold the list, after Berkeley's « multiple digital filter options ».

source.quote: FiiO's own parameters page, read 2026-11-24. « Hardware solution »: « SoC: ESP32-S3, DAC: ES9039Q2M*2, USB decoding: XU316, AMP: OPA1642*2 + TPA6120A*2 ». « Max. supported sampling rate » rows: « USB decoding: 768kHz/32bit; DSD512 »; « Coaxial decoding: 192kHz/24bit; DSD64 »; « Optical decoding: 96kHz/24bit »; « Coaxial output: 96kHz/24bit (USB decoding only) ». device_settings.why: « Oversampling setting: OS/NOS ». A two-position switch, stated as a specification row rather than buried in copy. In OS the device applies its own oversampling; in NOS it runs at the rate it is given. Auto exists to do that work with a filter we designed and can account for, so the device's stage belongs out of the path. This is also what makes correctable true: the field applies « only for devices doing direct DSD or NOS PCM ».

data.chip: Three parts, each with the role its maker gives it: TWO AK4493SEQ converters (AKM), one per channel - « The left and right channels are each equipped with an efficient high-performance AK4493SEQ » - an XMOS XUF208 as the USB interface, called « Decoder » by FiiO, and a « Dual THX AAA 788+ » amplifier stage. Exactly the case for a chip model that carries a ROLE per part: the converter, the interface and the amplifier are three different things and only the first is the conversion stage.

open_doubt.text: FiiO names four inputs for this device and rates none of them, and this catalogue cannot record « this input exists » without also recording a ceiling. An input block with no fields would be the honest shape and reads as noise; leaving it out loses the fact that the device HAS an optical input at all. Found while populating from makers' own pages, which is where it matters: a maker is free to publish the silicon and skip the rates, and this one did.

device_settings.why: The row « All to DSD » is supported and optional. Left OFF: Auto's whole purpose is to choose the format and rate reaching the conversion stage, and a device-side conversion to DSD would redo that work with a resampler we did not design and cannot account for. Turn it on only for a listener who prefers it and is not using Auto.

data.chip: « the latest generation AKM 4490 chip, which features 32-bit processing ».

device_settings.why: « 4 different DAC filter settings to tailor playback performance to personal preference ». A count and no names - the ninth maker in three days to do it. No value can be recorded. The AK4490's own filter menu is well known to have names; this page does not give them.

source.quote: Grace Design's own page for the m900, read 2026-11-25. « USB supported sample rates »: « 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, 176.4, 192, 352.8, 384kHz ». Features: « Asynchronous USB interface for jitter free computer audio playback, supports up to 384kHz PCM and 256x DSD »; « USB, S/PDIF and Toslink digital inputs, supports up to 192kHz (Toslink up to 96kHz) »; « 4 different DAC filter settings to tailor playback performance to personal preference ». Converter: « The m900 DAC uses the latest generation AKM 4490 chip, which features 32-bit processing ». The spec table gives no bit depth. Measurements are taken at the analogue output rather than for the D/A path alone: « THD+N at Maximum Volume, 1kHz, 22Hz-22kHz BW » with « @1.0V out, no load <0.002% », and « Dynamic Range ... 20-22kHz bandwidth 112 dB » / « 115 dB » A-weighted. No DSD figure is given for S/PDIF or Toslink. No terms-of-use page exists on the site; the footer carries the ordinary copyright line.

data._corrected: Filed under AKM until 2026-11-20 with no source naming any chip. It is ESS. The kernel's quirk table had said so all along - vendor 0x292b is commented "Gustard/Ess based devices" - and that comment was dismissed here as too vague to overturn a record. It was not vague; the record was unsourced. The two Gustard records now sit on two different families, which is why this brand carries none.

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.

open_doubt.device_level_kept: family, dsd_direct, analog_filter and correctable stay: the quote reaches the chip and its DSD behaviour, which is exactly what it talks about.
open_doubt.device_level_resolution: The DEVICE-level ceilings went the same way as the per-input ones, and for a reason that needs no judgement: this claim's quoted source carries NO figure at all - it reads « All iFi DACs that support DSD and are using TI/BB chipset » and « TI/BB DAC chips only support bit-perfect DSD playback ». It supports a chip family and a DSD behaviour, and nothing about a rate. The figures it was carrying (768 kHz, DSD512) were the Pro iDSD's, as the withdrawn per-input claim said in its own words. Withdrawing the per-input ceilings and keeping the device-level ones would have left the record LOOKING reviewed while still asserting one model's rates for the range.
evidence_kept: iFi Pro iDSD manual, read 2026-11-20, which states it plainly: « Inputs other than USB are currently limited to maximum sample rates of 192kHz PCM and DSD64 via DoP », against USB at 768 kHz and DSD1024.
open_doubt.resolution: The per-input ceilings were WITHDRAWN on 2026-11-24, on the claim's own confession: its source ended with « This record is the range's catch-all and the figures are the Pro iDSD's; the Neo and micro models were not documented per input. » A source that says it does not cover the subject is evidence against the claim it carries.
open_doubt.text: The family here is read from a conditional sentence: "All iFi DACs that support DSD and are using TI/BB chipset" describes the ones that use that silicon rather than claiming the range does. This record is the brand's catch-all, so it asserts the chip for every iFi converter on evidence that does not go that far.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: A per-model record (ifi/pro-idsd) carrying them. The quoted sentence is unusually clean evidence and should not be lost on the way.

device_settings.why: FIVE filters, all NAMED, in a specification row: « Bit-Perfect/Bit-Perfect+/Gibbs Transient Optimised/Apodising/Transient Aligned ». Bit-Perfect is the one to prefer and the name says why - it is the setting that applies no interpolation of the device's own, which is what Auto needs when it has already chosen the rate and the filter. The other four are real choices and worth knowing: « Gibbs Transient Optimised » targets the overshoot a brick-wall filter produces, « Apodising » is the designed-to-discard-the-source's-own-ringing family, and « Transient Aligned » is the same idea as Chord's WTA. This is the most filter choice any record in the catalogue offers.

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.

device_settings.why: In OS mode this converter oversamples EVERYTHING by sixteen to 705.6 or 768 kHz with its own filter. In NOS mode it runs at the rate it is given and applies none. Auto exists to do that work with a filter we designed and can account for, so the device's own stage should be out of the path - the same reasoning as the rate threshold that bypasses Chord's interpolation stage, reached here by a front-panel setting instead of by a rate.

data.chip: Not named. The body says the digital section performs « ein synchrones Re-Sampling und eine Delta-Sigma-Konversion in ein hochpraezises 1-bit-Signal (DSD) », so the conversion stage is fed a 1-bit DSD stream the device makes itself.

device_settings.why: « Re-Sampling: 180 dB Dynamik, 32 bit Aufloesung, bit-perfekt oder DSD » - the owner chooses between a bit-perfect path and conversion to DSD. Bit-perfect is the setting: Auto has already chosen the rate and the filter, and the device's own conversion to DSD would redo that work with a resampler we did not design. Note what the choice implies - on this device the PCM path can be left untouched, which the body text alone would not have told you.

source.quote: Linn's own page for the Klimax DSM, read 2026-11-25. Self-description: « Network music player and integrated pre-amplifier with inputs for additional digital and analogue sources ». Key features: « Supports formats up to 24-bit 384kHz with the addition of DSD256 »; « Distortion-free digital volume control ». Specification: « Resolution » « Up to 24-bit/384kHz »; « Audio Formats » « FLAC, Apple Lossless, WAV, DSD (64/128/256), MP3, WMA (except lossless), AIFF, AAC, OGG »; « Inputs » listing HDMI x4 and HDMI eARC x1 on the AV variant, Toslink x1, SPDIF x2 (one configurable as an output), USB Type B x1, balanced XLR x1 and two pairs of RCA - WITH NO RATE ON ANY OF THEM; « Exakt Link » x2; « Ethernet » x1; « Optical Ethernet » « x1 (SFP socket) ». source.quote: Linn's own page for the Majik DSM, read 2026-11-25. Self-description: « All-in-one network music player with integrated stereo power amplifier ». Key features: « Supports formats up to high-resolution 24-bit/384kHz ». device_settings.why: The page offers « DSD256 upsampling option for all files » and « PCM 384kHz upsampling option for all files », and « Upsampling and downsampling to every supported format up to DSD256/PCM384 ». Left OFF: Auto's whole purpose is to choose the format and rate reaching the conversion stage, and a device-side resampler would redo that work with a filter we did not design and cannot account for. Turn it on only for a listener who prefers it and is not using Auto. Same reasoning as FiiO's « All to DSD ».

device_settings.why: The page offers « DSD256 upsampling option for all files » and « PCM 384kHz upsampling option for all files », and « more flexible upsampling options for every supported format ». Left OFF: Auto's whole purpose is to choose the format and rate reaching the conversion stage, and a device-side resampler would redo that work with a filter we did not design and cannot account for. Turn it on only for a listener who prefers it and is not using Auto. Same reasoning as FiiO's « All to DSD ».

device_settings.why: The page offers « DSD256 upsampling option for all files » and « PCM 384kHz upsampling option for all files », and « Every calculation and filter tailored specifically for X2 ». Left OFF: Auto's whole purpose is to choose the format and rate reaching the conversion stage, and a device-side resampler would redo that work with a filter we did not design and cannot account for. Turn it on only for a listener who prefers it and is not using Auto. Same reasoning as FiiO's « All to DSD ».

device_settings.why: Four options, named: « Balanced, Natural, Dynamic Music, Dymanic Voice ». « Balanced » is the one to prefer - the other three are voicings aimed at material types, and Auto's job is to deliver the signal rather than to characterise it. The page also offers « Filter 1, 2 Selectable » and « Dither 1, 2, Off », whose effects it never describes, so no value is recorded for those two.

data._kind_is_wrong_here_and_there_is_no_righ: The maker calls it « a streaming preamplifier that unites analog with digital ». It streams over network and Wi-Fi, converts, preamplifies, and carries « 6 analog inputs ... plus 1 dedicated phono input for turntables ». kind takes one value and this catalogue knows two: dac and network_player. `dac` is recorded because the conversion stage is what this database is FOR, and the record therefore says nothing about the streaming half, the analogue half or the phono stage. Sharpest case yet of a gap already noted: kind is a single value where makers build one box that is three things.
data.chip: No part number and no maker. « 8-channel, 32-bit/384kHz PCM/DSD, Quad Balanced » - eight converter channels serving two output channels, four per side in a balanced arrangement. The page never says whose silicon it is, nor whether it is bought, discrete or an FPGA.

open_doubt.device_level_outcome: KEPT for now, and the reason is not that the figures are doubtful - the quote names « up to 384/24 and DSD256 » for one Merging Hapi, so they are supported. The defect is the SUBJECT, not the number: this record stands for every generation and every fitted card under one model name. Withdrawing the figures would lose true facts about a real unit. The fix is to key records by generation and card, which this doubt has asked for since 2026-11-20, and it is an identity question rather than a withdrawal.
evidence_kept: Merging Hapi MkII specifications, read 2026-11-20: 44.1 to 384 kHz PCM plus DSD64, DSD128 and DSD256 over the network.
open_doubt.resolution: The per-input ceiling was WITHDRAWN on 2026-11-24. The Hapi is MODULAR: its ceilings follow the card fitted, not the model name, so a single figure under the model is a claim the hardware does not support. The claim's own source named the generation it came from - the MkII specifications - while this doubt records that the MkIII's standard cards stop at 192 kHz.
open_doubt.text: The Hapi is MODULAR and its ceilings follow the card fitted, not the model name: on the MkIII the standard I/O cards stop at 192 kHz while the premium card reaches 352.8 and 384 kHz with DSD256. The figure recorded here is the MkII's. Third device in this catalogue whose model name does not determine its capability, after MSB's plug-in USB modules and the variants of the RME ADI-2 and the Schiit Yggdrasil.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: Records keyed by generation and fitted card, not by model name. Same shape as MSB's plug-in USB modules and the Schiit Yggdrasil variants, which this doubt already lists.

data._corrected: Renommee le 23/11/2026, de 'mola_mola' a 'mola_mola_generique'. La cle nommait un modele que la fiche ne revendique pas : son `model` est "unknown", donc c'est le fourre-tout de la marque. Rien ne lisait la cle - le moteur lit le champ - mais quiconque ouvrait ce fichier y lisait une precision qui n'existe pas. Le suffixe _generique est celui que portaient deja les autres fourre-tout.

data.chip: No part number, and the maker says why: « We decided to design, from the ground up, a discrete DAC » with « circuits and digital algorithms that were entirely developed in house ». The stage is « a discrete 32-stage FIR DAC and a single-stage 4th order filtering I/V converter », fed noise-shaped PWM at 3.125 MHz/32 bits.

source.quote: Mola Mola's own page for the Tambaqui, read 2026-11-24. OPERATING PRINCIPLE: « PWM DAC with 32-stage discrete analogue FIR output stage. Avoids 'sigma delta' tones and 'R2R' glitch and low-level linearity errors. » and « Asynchronous upsampling to 3.125MHz/32 bit. 7-th order noise shaper clearing 80kHz band. Each input rate has an optimized upsampling filter chain. » SUPPORTED FORMATS: « PCM up to 384kHz/32 bits (>192kHz and >24 bits via USB and Roon only) » and « DoP and Native DSD up to quad speed (USB and Roon only) ». I/O: « Optical (Toslink) », « S/PDIF (Cinch) », « AES/EBU (XLR) », « USB type B », « Ethernet (Roon Ready) », « Bluetooth (SBC, AAC, APTX, LDAC) », « IBIS over HDMI », « Balanced output (XLR) », « Headphone output (6.3mm Jack, Balanced XLR 4pin) ». PERFORMANCE: « Signal to Noise Ratio: 130dB »; « THD, IMD: not measurable (estimated -140dB) »; « Bandwidth: Up to 80kHz (apodizing response) »; « Integrated jitter: <1ps from 10Hz upwards, <300fs from 1kHz upwards ». Body text: « The converter is a two board stack. On the first board, all incoming digital audio is upsampled to 3.125MHz/32 bits and converted to noise shaped PWM. On the other board are two mono DACs, in which a discrete 32-stage FIR DAC and a single-stage 4th order filtering I/V converter, convert the PWM into analogue with a breathtaking 130dB SNR. This is near the theoretical limit for 24-bit files and far beyond that of even quad-speed DSD. »; « With the addition of a lossless digital volume control and headphone outputs »; « The Mola Mola Tambaqui is Roon Ready certified! »; « Responding to popular demand, Mola Mola launched the famous discrete DAC from the Makua as a separate unit. » The companion page https://www.mola-mola.nl/dac.php adds: « We decided to design, from the ground up, a discrete DAC »; « circuits and digital algorithms that were entirely developed in house »; and that the same two-board converter « fits into one of the option slots in the preamp ». Self-description: « Tambaqui - the DAC that Stands Alone ».

This is near the theoretical limit for 24-bit files and far beyond that of even quad-speed DSD. »; « With the addition of a lossless digital volume control and headphone outputs »; « The Mola Mola Tambaqui is Roon Ready certified! »; « Responding to popular demand, Mola Mola launched the famous discrete DAC from the Makua as a separate unit. » The companion page https://www.mola-mola.nl/dac.php adds: « We decided to design, from the ground up, a discrete DAC »; « circuits and digital algorithms that were entirely developed in house »; and that the same two-board converter « fits into one of the option slots in the preamp ». Self-description: « Tambaqui - the DAC that Stands Alone ».

open_doubt.device_level_kept: family and the ladder description stay - that is what the sentence actually says. dsd_direct was already `to_be_measured`.
open_doubt.device_level_resolution: The whole of this record's evidence is one sentence - « it is an R2R DAC (and thus native PCM) » - and it names no rate, no DSD format and no transport. It carried 768 kHz and DSD256 anyway. This doubt already said no per-input figure would be true of every unit sold under this name, because the USB input is a plug-in card; the same is true of a device-level figure, which is why none is left. Nothing here needed a judgement about over-reach: the evidence rule alone disposes of it.
open_doubt.text: MSB converters are MODULAR: the USB input is a plug-in card, so a given unit's ceiling depends on which module is fitted rather than on the model name. A review of the Discrete describes one with 768 kHz and DSD512 over USB while the fixed coaxial, optical and XLR inputs sit far lower. No per-input figure is recorded here because none would be true of every unit sold under this name - a third shape of the same problem, after a model that spans chips and a model that is a part.

data.chip: « 2x ES9038Q2M (dual mono) with 8x digital filter ».

device_settings.why: « Oversampling Bypass » is a named feature beside « Switchable Upsampling » and « Selectable Digital Filters ». Switching the oversampling out puts the device's own interpolation stage out of the path, which is what Auto needs and what makes `correctable` true. The eight PCM filters only matter if the bypass is off.

« For PCM signals, the M8x DAC has eight selectable digital filters » and not one is named - the tenth maker in three days to publish a count and withhold the list. The Topping DX1 II's manual names eight of what is very probably the same ESS menu, and they are NOT copied here.

source.quote: MUSICIAN Audio Technology's own PRODUCT page for the Aquarius, read 2026-11-25 with curl. « Sampling Mode: Non-Oversampling NOS / Oversampling OS »; « Technical Highlights / Proprietary R2R + DSD Architecture / True balanced 24BIT R2R + 6BIT DSD (32 steps FIR Filters) / Adopt 0.005% precision resistance Constant temperature twin crystal oscillator design »; « Proprietary USB Audio Solution via STM32F446 Advanced AMR Based MCU »; « Digital Signal Processing via FPGA »; « Licensed Thesycon USB Driver For Windows Platform ». Also « O-type single crystal copper transformer », « FIFO Buffer », « Driverless On Mac & Linux ».

data.chip: « DELPHINUS R2R DAC » is all the page says of the converter - no ladder depth, no resistor tolerance, no part number.

device_settings.why: « h. OS/NOS: Lit for native sampling, unlit for oversampling. » A front-panel indicator with two states, and the maker states the polarity - lit means native, which is the non-oversampled path. That is a selectable mode and the precondition `correctable` requires, established from the panel legend rather than from a spec line.

« g. FILTER: Fast/Slow ﬁlter selection. » A fast/slow digital filter choice, which NO OTHER MUSICIAN model offers - the others have the NOS mode and a fixed 32-step FIR. Two named positions, which is a complete list.

source.quote: MUSICIAN Audio Technology's own page for the Delphinus, read 2026-11-25 with curl. The page is headed « DELPHINUS R2R DAC / Digital Player » and the home page links it under TWO names, « Delphinus » and « MDP-2 ». Front-panel legend, verbatim: « g. FILTER: Fast/Slow ﬁlter selection. »; « h. OS/NOS: Lit for native sampling, unlit for oversampling. »; « Indicator Light Guide / a. Input Source Indicators: COAX, OPT, AES, USB, I2S. When a speciﬁc input source is selected, the corresponding indicator will illuminate. / b. Sampling rate indicator lights: 44.1K, 48K. These indicator lights indicate the sampling rate of the current input audio signal. (K: Sampling rate in kHz) / c. Multiplier Indicator Lights: 1X, 2X, 4X, 8X. The corresponding indicator shows the current audio signal's multiplication factor. / d.Audio Format Indicator: Lit for DSD, unlit for PCM. / e. PHASE Indicator: Lit for inverted phase, unlit for in-phase. / f. SWAP: Swaps left and right channels in I2S during DSD mode. » The ﬁ and ﬀ ligatures are the page's own, pasted from a PDF. ABSENT: no maximum PCM rate, no bit depth, no DSD maximum, no native or DoP statement, no per-input ceiling, no formal input or output list, no dimensions, no ladder bit depth. The page carries 19 JPEGs at 1110 x 1110 px, from which no figure was read.

data.chip: « True balanced 24BIT R2R + 6BIT DSD (32 steps FIR Filters) » - a discrete ladder for PCM and a separate 6-bit path for DSD, with no part number because the ladder IS the converter. The only semiconductors named are the USB receiver, « STM32F446 Advanced AMR Based MCU », and an FPGA for « Digital Signal Processing » - neither converts.

device_settings.why: « Sampling Mode: Non-Oversampling NOS / Oversampling OS » - stated as a specification line, user-selectable. And the maker says what the OS path contains: « 32 steps FIR Filters ». So selecting NOS removes a named 32-step FIR from the signal path, which is the precondition `correctable` requires, with the filter it removes identified.

data.chip: « a fully balanced R2R circuit, high-speed multi-channel digital isolators, multiple sets of R2R array resistors and triggers, achieving precise D/A conversion » - the sentence binds the ladder to the conversion, so this is a genuine discrete-ladder claim. « high-precision manual matching of 0.1% resistors », against 0.005% on the Aquarius and Taurus - a per-model difference, not a conflict. FPGA for « Digital Signal Processing », USB via « STM32F446 ». No part number, and none exists anywhere on the site.

data.chip: No converter part number. « A high-performance FPGA performs all internal calculations », in a « dual-mono topology ». The « 8-core X-Mos chip » named on the page is the USB RECEIVER, not the converter, and the « two NOS military JAN5963 tubes » are the output stage.

source.quote: Nagra's own page for the HD DAC X, read 2026-11-24. On the signal path: « Every input signal is converted into DSD 256 format (11.2 MHz sample rate). » On the processing: « A high-performance FPGA performs all internal calculations. »; « Like the HD PREAMP, it uses a dual-mono topology. »; « Ultra-high precision and ultra-low jitter clocks are used in this new Nagra HD DAC X. » Technical specification, « Digital inputs: » « 1x AES/EBU, 2x S/PDIF, 2x NAGRA-LINK, 1x Optical, 1x Audio USB (UCA2) », and in the body « The HD DAC X features AES-EBU, S/P-DIF on both RCA and BNC and 2x Nagra Link single-mode ST-1 optical inputs to receive future Nagra high resolution sources. »; « The USB input uses a proprietary software designed around an 8-core X-Mos chip. » On the output stage: « two NOS military JAN5963 tubes (one per channel) » and « This stage makes use of a cathodyne output design. » Self-description: « The HD DAC X is a step forward from the world-acclaimed Nagra HD DAC. » The page also carries « Specifications may change without notice ». The companion HD line page (https://www.nagraaudio.com/the-high-end-collection/the-hd-line/) says « Capable of DSD 256 and DXD ».

open_doubt.text: What performs the conversion. The page names « A high-performance FPGA » for « all internal calculations » and « two NOS military JAN5963 tubes » for the output, and nothing in between. Every input becomes DSD256, so something turns a 1-bit stream at 11.2 MHz into analogue, and the page does not say what. technology was briefly recorded as fpga and withdrawn (see the claim's own note): Rockna demonstrates on one device that an FPGA can do all the digital work while a discrete ladder converts.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: The Nagra HD DAC X user manual, linked from the product page and not read. Do NOT resolve it from « performs all internal calculations »: that sentence has now been shown, on another maker's page, to be compatible with a separate conversion stage.

source.quote: NuPrime's own page for the DAC-8, read 2026-11-25 in full, input list: « USB : Type B 2.0 Hi-Speed, Windows OS : data stream up to 384KHz/24Bit and Native DSD 256. »; « USB : Type B 2.0 Hi-Speed, Mac / Lunix OS : data stream up to 384KHz/24Bit and DOP DSD 128. » - the misspelling « Lunix » is the page's; « IIS/DSD : Supports PCM 44.1KHz ~ 384KHz/32Bit and DSD 64 ~ DSD 256 data streams. »; « OPTICAL : Supports PCM 44.1KHz ~ 192KHz/24Bit and DOP 64. »; « COAXIAL : Supports PCM 44.1KHz ~ 384KHz/24Bit and DOP 64 and 128. »; « EXTENSION : Supports PCM 44.1KHz ~ 192KHz/24Bit. » The specification text names NO converter. A third-party review quoted on the page says « Featuring the ESS ES9018Q2C chip and NuPrime's custom SRC IC for DSP processing ». A volume FAQ says « The DAC's analog output ... go through a low noise and low distortion resistance ladder circuit design (implemented as an IC) ». No digital filter, oversampling or NOS row.

open_doubt.text: What the PSRC resampler does by default. « NuPrime PSRC IC chip provides sample rate up/down conversion processing, from PCM 44.1kHz to PCM 768kHz and DSD64 to DSD512 (including PCM to/from DSD). » A resampler that goes up, down, and across the PCM/DSD boundary in BOTH directions, sitting between the inputs and a pair of ESS9038Q2M. The page describes a CAPABILITY and never says what it does when the owner has chosen nothing, nor whether the owner can choose at all. So neither pcm_reconverted_to_dsd nor dsd_reconverted_to_pcm is written, and no device_settings entry either. Third shape of this question in two days: Nagra, APL HiFi and Mola Mola convert unconditionally and say so; FiiO's R7 and R9 offer « All to DSD » as a switch; this one states a capability with no default. The first two shapes are recordable and this one is not.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: One sentence from NuPrime about the default state of the PSRC, or a menu listing from the manual. Do NOT resolve it from the chip's capability list: a resampler that CAN convert PCM to DSD is not a device that DOES.

device_settings.why: « the PCM up-sampling option, which when the setting is enabled allows 16/44.1 and 24/48 kHz signals to be up-sampled to 24/88.2 kHz and 24/96 kHz respectively ». A setting, off by implication since the maker calls enabling it a choice. Left off for the reason applied to every optional resampler here - LUMIN's, FiiO's, Pro-Ject's, Aurender's: Auto has already chosen the rate and designed the filter.

device_settings.why: This device's inputs ARE its modules: AES3/S-PDIF on DB25, Pro Tools HD, Pro Tools HDX, FireWire, and formerly DSD over SDIF. What a given chassis accepts depends on which cards are in its two digital slots, and no record can say which.

source.quote: Prism Sound's own pages for the Dream ADA-8XR, read 2026-11-25 - the overview, the tech-specs page and the modules page, where the per-module figures live. Overview: « the goals of ultimate sound quality, unbeatable performance and un-matched versatility have been realised in a modular multi-channel, 24-bit 192kHz-capable format. » Synchronization block: « Internal - 32, 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, 176.4, 192 kHz +/-25ppm »; « Each path can be separately synchronized. » The AES3 module: « The module can accommodate extended sample rates (up to 192kHz) in Split96 (two-wire) or high-speed (one-wire) modes »; « Wordlength - 16, 20 or 24-bit »; « One-wire or two-wire ("Split96") input and output modes supported @ 88.2, 96, 176.4 and 192kHz »; « AES3 mode: I/O impedance - 110 Ohm »; « S/PDIF mode: I/O impedance - 75 Ohm ». The Pro Tools modules: « supporting sample rates up to 192kHz » for both HD and HDX. source.quote: Prism Sound's own specification page for the Atlas, read 2026-11-25. The Digital Inputs, Digital Outputs and Synchronization sections are word-for-word identical to the Titan's: « Sample rates supported - S/PDIF (2 channel): 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, 176.4 and 192kHz / ADAT (8 channel) 44.1 and 48kHz / ADAT S/MUX (4 channel): 88.2 and 96kHz »; « Word-length - 24 bit »; « System sample rates - 44.1 / 48 / 88.2 / 96 / 176.4 / 192kHz ». Rear Panel adds: « MIDI I/O - 2 x 5 Pin DIN sockets (in and out) » and « MDIO Expansion Slot - For alternative digital multi-channel I/O », beside the same « Digital inputs - 1 x RCA / 1 x TOSLINK for S/PDIF or ADAT Optical input » and « USB port - 1 x USB 2 port ». DSD appears nowhere. No converter chip part number is named, no digital filter name or count is given, and no oversampling bypass is offered - a grep across every captured Prism Sound page for AK4, ES90, CS43, PCM17, WM87, Sabre, Burr-Brown, Asahi Kasei and Cirrus Logic returned zero matches.

USB Inputs section: « Interface protocol - USB Audio Device Class 2.0 (UAC2) »; « Audio formats supported - PCM audio of up to 32 bit word length at sampling rates of 44k1, 48k, 88k2, 96k, 176k4, 192k, 352k8, 384k and DSD64, DSD128 in DoP frame (for fs>192k see note at foot of page). » S/PDIF Inputs section: « Interface formats - S/PDIF (RCA and TOSLINK); RCA also accepts AES3-ID »; « Audio formats - PCM audio of up to 24 bit word length at sampling rates of 44k1, 48k, 88k2, 96k, 176k4, 192k and DSD64 in DoP frame »; « Channel Status - ignored ». Note at the foot: « From its USB interface, CALLIA can play audio at sampling rates greater than 192kHz. At these higher rates a proprietary, high performance decimation filter is used to reduce the sampling rate by a factor of 2. For example, 384kHz will be converted down to 192kHz. » Overview page: « CALLIA supports linear PCM in 2's complement binary coding and, using the "DSD over PCM" (DOP) protocol, DSD at the original bit-rate (DSD64) and also at 2 x the original rate (DSD128). »; « On the S/P-DIF inputs, DOP can also be used, but only at the original DSD bit rate (DSD64) as these connections do not have enough bandwidth for DSD128. »; « The ASIO native DSD format is not currently supported. » Synchronization: « Clock recovery technology - Prism Sound CleverClox hybrid PLL »; « Synchronization sources: - Local or S/PDIF input (automatic selection) ». Rear panel: « S/PDIF inputs | RCA coaxial and TOSLINK optical formats »; « USB port | USB 2.0 B type device socket ». No converter chip part number, no filter name or count, and no oversampling bypass appears anywhere.

source.quote: Prism Sound's own specification page for the Dream DA-2, read 2026-11-25 on the legacy host - this product is not on the current prismsound.io site at all, and survives only here, where the navigation still lists « Dream DA-2 - Premium 2 channel D/A converter ». Rear Panel: « Digital inputs - 1 x TOSLINK for S/PDIF input »; « Digital output - 1 x TOSLINK for S/PDIF output »; « USB port - 1 x USB type B receptacle » - and there is NO Wordclock row at all and no RCA. Digital Inputs: « Formats supported - S/PDIF TOSLINK »; « Sample rates supported - 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, 176.4 and 192kHz »; « Channel Status: - Ignored »; « Word-length - 24 bit »; « Sample-rate converter (SRC) - Selectable at S/PDIF input; allowing input at any sample rate ». Synchronization: « System sample rates - 44.1 / 48 / 88.2 / 96 / 176.4 / 192kHz »; « Sync sources: Master - local, Wordclock, DI (S/PDIF input) or ADAT ». Rear Panel: « Digital inputs - 1 x RCA / 1 x TOSLINK for S/PDIF or ADAT Optical input; (RCA can operate as AES3 input using XLR-RCA adapter) »; « Wordclock - 2 x BNC sockets, output and input (75R) »; « USB port - 1 x USB 2 port ». DSD, DoP and SACD appear nowhere on the page. No converter chip part number is named, no digital filter name or count is given, and no oversampling bypass is offered - a grep across every captured Prism Sound page for AK4, ES90, CS43, PCM17, WM87, Sabre, Burr-Brown, Asahi Kasei and Cirrus Logic returned zero matches.

data.chip: « 2x ESS9038Q2M (dual mono - 32bit/768kHz/DSD512) ».

device_settings.why: « High Quality optionally selectable upsampling of PCM and/or MQA content with propriatory filtering ». Optional and the owner's choice, so left off for the same reason as LUMIN's and FiiO's: Auto has already chosen the rate and designed the filter, and a device-side resampler with a proprietary filter would redo that work with something we cannot account for.

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.

data._two_editions_the_schema_cannot_tell_apa: One page, two products: « RD-0 (used in Signature - 27 bit structure) and RD-1 (used in Edition - 26 bit structure) », with two output blocks measuring 132 dB and 122 dB SNR. Facts DO distinguish them, so `edition` is a stretch - and every field this catalogue HOLDS is identical for both: same inputs, same rates, same filters, same NOS switch, same ladder topology. What separates them is the module's bit structure, THD, SNR and output voltage, none of which the schema has. So the two names resolve here, as editions, and the reason is recorded: not missing evidence, but evidence about things the catalogue does not model.
data.chip: No part number, because the modules are the maker's own: « dedicated dac modules called RD-0 (used in Signature - 27 bit structure) and RD-1 (used in Edition - 26 bit structure) ... sharing a discrete sign-magnitude hybrid ladder topology, driven by a complex algorythm which is embedded into their own FPGA ». TWO FPGAs, doing two different jobs: one on the main board for « all building blocks ... concernig digital processing », one inside each module driving the ladder. The conversion itself is the discrete ladder, not either FPGA.

device_settings.why: « The filters can be switched off for NOS operation. » Said by the maker, in a menu, with no condition. Without it the device « upsamples any material with a fixed rate of 16x » and decodes at 768 or 705.6 kHz through a 5k-tap Parks-McClellan filter of its own. Auto exists to do that work with a filter we designed and can account for, so the device's stage belongs out of the path. This is also what makes correctable true: the field applies « only for devices doing direct DSD or NOS PCM », and this is the first device in the catalogue whose maker offers NOS in so many words.

Three named variations: « linear, minimum and hybrid phase ». The maker describes each by its impulse response - linear splits « the ringing energy (Gibb's overshoot) ... equally split before and after impulse », minimum « shows all this energy after impulse », and the hybrid « exhibing very low overshoot before the impulse ». Hybrid is recorded as the setting because pre-ringing is the artefact apodising filters exist to remove. It applies only if NOS is NOT selected, which is the first ordered pair of settings in the catalogue.

source.quote: Rockna Audio's own page for the Wavedream DAC, read 2026-11-24 in a browser (the Technical Specs panel is a hidden tab, invisible to a plain text extraction). DIGITAL INPUTS: « S/PDIF 24bit 44.1-192k PCM , DoP DSD64 »; « AES/EBU 24bit 44.1-192k PCM, DoP DSD64 »; « USB 32bit 44.1-384k PCM, DSD64-512 »; « HD-Link1 (LVDS) 32bit 44.1-384k PCM, DSD64-512 »; « HD-Link2 (LVDS) 32bit 44.1-384k PCM, DSD64-512 ». D/A CONVERSION: « For the effective D/A conversion stage we developed dedicated dac modules called RD-0 (used in Signature - 27 bit structure) and RD-1 (used in Edition - 26 bit structure). Modules themselves are complex pieces of technology, sharing a discrete sign-magnitude hybrid ladder topology, driven by a complex algorythm which is embedded into their own FPGA. »; « Currently RD-0/1 can sustain a maximum sample rate of 6 MHz, which is the industry's maximum sample rate specified for a audio dac. »; « The output of the dac modules is un-buffered ». Minimum phase type shows all this energy after impulse, while our special hyrid phase filter has a combined response between linear and minimum, exhibing very low overshoot before the impulse. » EXTRA MENU FEATURES: « The filter select feature - discussed above. The filters can be switched off for NOS operation. »; « The clock setting - there are 2 modes of the digital PLL response, stream and local. »; « Dither - to improve R2R ladder linearity, ultrasonic dither is applied on the last 4 bits from the digital 24-bit word. »; « The Wavedream has a 256 steps volume control which allows direct connection of a power amplifier. The volume control has 0.5 dB steps ». OUTPUT STAGE: « the output stage is totally discrete and acts as a high-speed buffer », « we combined j-fet & bipolar devices into a class A design ». OUTPUTS (Wavedream Signature): « S/N ratio (0 dB): 132 dB ». OUTPUTS (Wavedream Edition): « S/N ratio (0 dB): 122 dB ». data.chip: « AKM's flagship DAC chip the AK4497 », with « The 2nd XMOS solution » as the USB receiver.

device_settings.why: SIX positions, all named, and they are the AKM set - Sharp Roll-off, Slow Roll-off, Short Delay Sharp, Short Delay Slow, Super Slow, Low Dispersion Short Delay - not the ESS seven. The filter menu follows the converter, which is why this record's list differs from every other Sabaj record's: this is the one AKM model of the A-series. Same six names as the Shanling EC Zero AKM's AK4493S.
« dF1 (DSD filter 1) » and « dF2 (DSD filter 2) » - two positions, named by number only, with no cut-off frequency and no description.

data.chip: « 2 pieces of ESS technology high-end digital-analog chip ES9038Q2M », with « The second-generation XMOS solution ».

device_settings.why: Seven positions, all named - and note the naming is idiosyncratic: « FL1 (Fixed minimum phase fast roll-off) » and « FL7 (Brickwall Mixing Filter) » are not how the A20d original names its FL1 and FL7, although both are seven-position ESS menus. Quoted as printed rather than normalised to the usual list.
« DPLL 1~9 » here, where the A20d original offers 1~15. Nine positions, not fifteen.

USB  1bit，16~32bit / Optical/Coaxial  1bit，16~24bit »; « Sampling rate ... USB  PCM 44.1~768kHz / USB  DSD  2.8224~22.5792MHz / Optical/Coaxial  PCM  44.1~192kHz / Optical/Coaxial  DSD DSD64(DoP) »; « Input ... USB / Optical / Coaxial / Bluetooth »; « Output ... 6.35mm headphone/4.4mm headphone/XLR/RCA »; « USB Spec ... USB1.1，USB2.0(Asynchronization) ». data.chip: « The top performance D/A chip ES9038PRO from ESS Technology », with « The high-performance power supply chip ES9311 » beside it and « XMOS XU-216 » as the USB receiver.

device_settings.why: SEVEN positions, all seven named with their characteristics spelled out - FL1 through FL7, from « Fast Roll-off linear phase » to « Brickwall filter ». This is the complete ESS list, which nine makers in four days have counted and refused to name. No NOS or bypass position.

« dPL 1~15, Lower for Better De-jitter » - the ESS phase-locked-loop bandwidth, fifteen positions. Not a filter: it sets how tightly the device tracks an incoming clock, and a lower setting rejects more jitter at the cost of locking to fewer sources.

Bit depth and sampling rate are given as SEPARATE per-input rows: « Bit depth / USB ... 1bit ~ 32bit / Optical/coaxial ... 16bit ~ 24bit »; « Sampling rate: / USB ... 44.1 ~ 768kHz / DSD64, DSD128, DSD256, DSD512 / Optical/coaxial ... 32 ~ 192kHz ». « Inputs ... USB / Optical / Coaxial / Bluetooth »; « Output ... Unbalanced / Balanced »; « USB transmission ... Asynchronous ». Features: « The top performance D/A chip ES9038PRO from ESS Technology; », « The high-performance power supply chip ES9311, the noise of ES9311 is as low as 1uVrms, to push ES9038PRO to the limit; », « XMOS XU-216, true 32bit audio processing, supports DoP and Native DSD, and reaches 32bit/768kHz and DSD512; », « All inputs support DSD streaming, including coaxial and optical (DoP64); ». MQA: « The A20d supports MQA decoding on the USB interface. » and in Chinese « A20d只有USB接口支持MQA解码，其它接口不支持! ». The rear-panel legend reads « 8 I2S input » and the INPUT menu reads « IN1 BLUETHOOTH / IN2 USB / IN3 OPTICAL / IN4 COAXIAL / IN5 I2S » - « BLUETHOOTH » is the manual's own spelling. The manual documents the I2S pinout and offers « I2S MODE  Nor (Normal) / INV (Inverted) » and « I2S DSD CHANNEL  L-r / r-L ». Features: « The top performance D/A chip ES9038PRO from ESS Technology; », « The high-performance power supply chip ES9311, the noise of ES9311 is as low as 1uVrms, to push ES9038PRO to the limit; », « XMOS XU-216, true 32bit audio processing, supports DoP and Native DSD, and reaches 32bit/768kHz and DSD512; », « All inputs support DSD streaming, including coaxial and optical (DoP64); ». MQA: « The A20d supports MQA decoding on the USB interface. » and in Chinese « A20d只有USB接口支持MQA解码，其它接口不支持! ». The rear-panel legend reads « 8 I2S input » and the INPUT menu reads « IN1 BLUETHOOTH / IN2 USB / IN3 OPTICAL / IN4 COAXIAL / IN5 I2S » - « BLUETHOOTH » is the manual's own spelling. The manual documents the I2S pinout and offers « I2S MODE  Nor (Normal) / INV (Inverted) » and « I2S DSD CHANNEL  L-r / r-L ». PCM FILTER: « FL1 (Fast Roll-off linear phase) », « FL2 (Slow Roll-off linear phase) », « FL3 (Fast Roll-off minimum phase) », « FL4 (Slow Roll-off minimum phase) », « FL5 (Apodizing, fast roll-off, linear phase) », « FL6 (Hybrid, fast roll-off, minimum phase) », « FL7 (Brickwall filter) ». « DPLL  dPL 1~15, Lower for Better De-jitter ». No NOS or oversampling-bypass mode.

data.chip: « ESS technology high-end digital-analog chip ES9038PRO », with « The second-generation XMOS solution » as the USB receiver.

device_settings.why: Six positions, all named: Fast Linear, Slow Linear, Fast Minimum, Apodizing, Fast Hybrid, Brickwall. Note there is no « Slow Minimum » here, where the A20d original and the D5 both have one - so this is a six-position subset of the usual ESS seven. No NOS or bypass.

Four positions named by cut-off: 47, 50, 60 and 70 kHz. The maker explains what they do: « Its function is to filter out the clutter outside the audio by means of digital operation » - digital, not analogue, unlike the VMV range's analogue DSD cut-offs.

« NORMAL mode, only use digital receiving chip to process SPDIF signal [...] PCM supports 44.1-192KHZ, DOP supports DSD64. » against « PROCESSOR mode, in this mode, the machine uses the XMOS processor to process the optical fiber coaxial signal, so that it can have powerful computing power and can handle MQA. » A setting that changes WHICH CHIP receives the S/PDIF input. The published per-socket ceiling belongs to NORMAL mode; what PROCESSOR mode accepts is not stated.

data.chip: « Flagship DAC chip AK4191+ AK4499EX » - a converter and its matching modulator as a pair, with « New 3rd generation XMOS XU-316 » as the USB receiver.

device_settings.why: SIX positions, all six NAMED: SHARP ROLL-OFF, SLOW ROLL-OFF, SHORT SHARP, SHORT SLOW, SUPER SLOW, LOW DISPERSION. No NOS or bypass position for PCM - so `correctable` is not written.
Two positions, « WIDE » and « NARROW » - an analogue reconstruction filter after the converter, not an interpolation filter, so it does not bear on `correctable`.

« When this function is opened, the DSD is not processed at all, and the output is directly output. » A DSD-only direct path, at the cost of volume control - the amplitude is fixed at about 3.7 Vrms. This is what the registered field `dsd_direct` describes, and that field is still planned, so the fact lives here. Note what it does NOT give: PCM still goes through one of the six filters, with no way out.

« SOUND 1(5.6M) / SOUND 2(5.6M) / SOUND 3(11M) / SOUND 4(11M) », glossed as « The AK4499EX operates at a sampling rate of 5.6448MHz » or « 11.2896MHz ». These are the CONVERTER'S INTERNAL operating rates, not anything an input accepts - a user-selectable internal rate, which is rarer than a filter menu and which no field can hold.

source.quote: Sabaj's own manual for the A3, A3.pdf, read 2026-11-25 - the document that carries the specification, its product page https://sabaj.com.cn/pages/manual-download (no product page exists) being image-only. The clearest per-socket split in the whole range, verbatim: « THD+N:  0.06% »; « SNR：  90dB »; « Channel separation:  80dB »; « USB compatibility:  Windows、Linux、Mac OS X »; « USB the highest sampling rate:  24bit/96kHz »; « Optical the highest sampling rate:  24bit/192kHz »; « Output power: 80W+80W（4Ω) »; « Consumption power:  50W »; « Standby power:  1W ». Inputs: « USB,3.5mm Analog,Blutooth,Optical totally 4 inputs. » - « Blutooth » is the manual's spelling. Rear-panel legend: « K USB input », « J Optical input », « L Bluetooth antenna », « M Analog input ». Input cycle order: « AUX→BT→USB→OPT ». NO coaxial input on this model, NO converter chip part number anywhere, NO DSD figure - DSD is not mentioned at all - and no digital filter menu: the menu is « Input source→EQ mode→Bass volume control→Treble volume control→ ».

source.quote: Sabaj's own manual for the A30a 2022, 2022_A30A.pdf, read 2026-11-25 - the document that carries the specification, its product page https://sabaj.com.cn/pages/manual-download (no product page exists) being image-only. « Inputs ... USB / Optical / Bluetooth /Coaxial / LINE IN »; « Bit depth ... USB  1bit， 16 ~ 32bit / Optical / Coaxial  1bit， 16 ~ 24bit »; « Sampling rate ... USB  PCM  44.1 ~ 768kHz / USB  DSD  2.8224-22.5792MHz / Optical / Coaxial  PCM  44.1 ~ 192kHz »; « Output power ... 200Wx2(4Ω) / 100Wx2(8Ω) ». NOTE that no DSD figure at all is given for optical or coaxial - the DSD row exists only under USB. INPUTS menu, which marks the analogue one explicitly: « AUX(ANALOG) / USB AUDIO / OPTICAL / COAXIAL / BLUETOOTH ». Rear panel: « 9 USB input », « 10 Optical input », « 11 Coaxial input », « 12 RCA input ». Features: « Using the latest DSP chip with ST high-power amplifier chip, carefully designed and debugged, its distortion is as low as 0.0008%; » and « The second generation XMOS solution, PCM sampling rate up to 32bit/768kHz; ». NO D/A converter part number is named anywhere in this manual - only « DSP chip », « ST high-power amplifier chip » and the XMOS USB receiver. No « native », no « DoP », no MQA, and no digital filter menu: the only audio-shaping menu is a 20-preset EQ list plus « Loudness 1 » to « Loudness 16 », which are not filters.

data.chip: « The top performance D/A chip ES9038PRO from ESS Technology », with « XMOS XU-208 ».

device_settings.why: Seven positions, all named, AND the maker states their scope: « these filters are only valid when playback PCM music ». That sentence is worth more than the list - it says the menu does not touch DSD, which on most pages a reader has to assume. No NOS or bypass position.

device_settings.why: « FLT1: Fast rolloff (Default), FLT2: Slow rolloff, FLT3: Minimum phase » - three positions, all named, and the maker says which is the DEFAULT. A published default is rarer than a published list and it tells a reader what the device does out of the box.

data.chip: « a standard delta-sigma modulator, in this case an ES9028 » (ESS), with Schiit's own time- and frequency-domain optimised filter ahead of it.

device_settings.setting: Mesh or NOS filter mode switching
device_settings.why: The maker offers the choice in its « Forkbeard Capabilities » list. In Mesh mode Schiit's own filter runs; in NOS it does not. Auto exists to do that work with a filter we designed and can account for, so the device's stage belongs out of the path - and NOS is the precondition `correctable` requires.

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.
data._corrected: This record was called "Yggdrasil" and carried a quote about ONE of its three variants. Schiit sells the Yggdrasil in three flavours on three different converters: the OG on Analog Devices AD5791 at 20 bits, Less is More on four TI DAC8812 at 16 bits, and More is Less on TI DAC11001 at 20 bits. Only the second is described here, and only the second is 16-bit - so the record's bits, its chip and its family were right for a device its own name did not identify. Renamed rather than generalised. The apparent contradiction between "16-bit TI DAC" and the ladder family was never one: all three are multibit ladder parts rather than delta-sigma, which is the whole point of Schiit's multibit line.
data.chip: Four TI DAC8812, 16-bit. The maker's multibit line uses ladder parts rather than delta-sigma; the other two Yggdrasil variants use Analog Devices AD5791 and TI DAC11001, both 20-bit.

source.quote: Schiit Audio's own page for the Yggdrasil +, read 2026-11-24. The page carries a separate spec block per variant. For the Yggdrasil LIM: « Inputs: Unison USB, AES/EBU XLR, RCA SPDIF, BNC SPDIF, Optical SPDIF » and « Input Capability: up to 24/192 for all inputs ». Conversion: « D/A Conversion IC: Texas Instruments DAC8812 x 4 (2 per channel, dual hardware balanced configuration) », with « proprietary Schiit time- and frequency-domain optimized digital filter implemented on Analog Devices SHARC DSP processor ». data.chip: The maker names the converter TWICE with two different part numbers on one page: « Cirrus Logic CS43918 » in the body and « Cirrus Logic CS43198 » in the specification list. Neither is picked. CS43198 is a part that exists; CS43918 is very probably its digits transposed - but guessing which of a maker's two spellings is the typo is exactly the interpretation this catalogue must not make silently.

device_settings.why: « PCM Filter: 0-4 », options « Fast Roll-Off/Slow Roll-Off/Low-latency Fast/Low-latency Slow/NOS » - five positions, all five NAMED, the fifth being non-oversampling. EC Play has no valves, so NOS is unambiguous here. One of the very few records in the catalogue where a maker both names its filters and offers a way to leave them out.

source.quote: Shanling's own announcement for the EC Play, read 2026-11-25, with its manual at /download/files/ECPlay.pdf; the product page /product/492 is image-only. Body: « And for fans of High-Resolution files, the USB DAC Mode is ready for Music up to 384 kHz and DSD256. » Specification: « USB DAC Support: 384kHz/32-bit, DSD256 »; « Amplifier: 2 x SGM8262-2 »; « Bluetooth Version: 6.0 / Bluetooth Receiver: LDAC/AAC/SBC / Bluetooth Transmitter: SBC »; « Supported discs: CD/CD-RW/CD-R »; « Frequency Response: CD Playback: 20 Hz-20,000 Hz / USB DAC: 20 Hz-40,000 Hz ». data.chip: « a modern 24bit R2R DAC » developed in-house, explicitly in the lineage of « the legendary PCM1704 DACs » - a discrete ladder with no part number, 24 bits deep while the input accepts 32. USB receiver « XMOS XU316 », Bluetooth « Qualcomm QCC5125 », line stage « OPA1612 ».

source.quote: Shanling's own announcement for the EH2, read 2026-11-25; the product page /product/468 is 25 image slices. « Specification: »: « Hi-Res Support USB: 768 kHz/32 bit, DSD 512 »; « Inputs: USB-C, Coaxial, Optical, Bluetooth »; « Outputs: 6.35mm & 4.4mm Headphone output, RCA & 4.4mm Line Output ». Body: « In-House developed DAC module is a big step for our audio engineers, creating a modern 24bit R2R DAC that follows the heritage of our old high-end designs based around the legendary PCM1704 DACs, such as the Shanling CD-T300 and HDCD-H24. »; « The USB input was upgraded Hi-Fi level to XMOS XU316 module, next to which we slotted both the coaxial and optical SPDIF inputs. And as an extra bonus, Qualcomm QCC5125 brings in Bluetooth V5.2 compatibility »; « Offering up to 4.3W @ 32Ohm on its 4.4mm balanced output … while its single-ended 6.35mm output brings 1.3W @ 32Ohm »; « Additional circuit was added for the RCA & 4.4mm Line-out / Pre-out, based around OPA1612, offering the pure R2R output ». No per-socket figure is given for coaxial, optical or Bluetooth.

Shanling's own MANUAL for the EH2, EH2.pdf, read 2026-11-25 - a separate document from the announcement. Its « Sampling Frequency Indicator / Showing current sampling frequency during playback » table, verbatim: « 44.1/48kHz - Blue »; « 64/88.2/96kHz - Green »; « 128/176.4/192kHz - Yellow »; « 352.8/384/705.6/768kHz - Purple »; « DSD64/128/256 - White »; « 44.1/48kHz (UAC 1.0) - Red ». source.quote: Shanling's own announcement for the EH3, read 2026-11-25, with its manual at /catlog/EH3.pdf; the product page /product/440 is 16 image slices. Verbatim, with its full surrounding sentence: « System includes the ability of independent local playback from USB Drive. Fully lossless playback directly on the DAC, without any need for a separate digital source or computer. Supporting all the major audio formats and Hi-Res files up to PCM 32/768 and DSD512. »; « For use as DAC, EH3 can be connected over USB, Optical, Coaxial or I2S HDMI. It can be also used as a pure amplifier thanks to a pair of RCA Analog inputs. »; « Utilizing flagship ESS ES9039SPRO 8-channel DAC with fully balanced amplifier based around four OPA1612. With in-house developed FPGA, KDS crystal oscillators and XMOS XU316 USB Chip »; « Offering up to 1 900 mW @ 32 Ohm // 205mW @ 300 Ohm in Single-Ended and 5 300 mW @ 32 Ohm // 700mW @ 300 Ohm in Balanced. »; « Connected over the high-quality I2S connection, using our new L8 cable, with All-to-DSD processing, making for the ultimate CD and MQA CD Playback. » The manual, under its own heading « USB Driver Playback »: « 1. It's recommended to use USB drivers formatted to FAT32. / 2. Drives up to 2TB are supported. / 3. Support up to PCM 768kHz and DSD512. » Its « USB DAC Mode » section that follows carries NO figure. Rear-panel labels: « Digital Coaxial Input », « Digital Optical Input », « USB DAC Input », « Digital IIS-LVDS Input », « Analog Input », plus a USB audio output and a USB external-storage port. The manual has no OS/NOS control.
