data.chip: « The high-end Shanling PRO R2R module », a discrete ladder with no part number, first used in the SCD3.3 SACD player and the SM1.3R streamer.

device_settings.why: « switch between OS (Oversampling) and NOS (Non-oversampling) data processing of DAC. Oversampling filter will process all audio at 352.8kHz. » The second sentence is rare and valuable: it says WHAT THE OVERSAMPLING PATH DOES. Almost every maker that offers a bypass describes only the bypass; this one states the rate everything is resampled to when the bypass is off, which is what an engine needs to decide whether to send 352.8 kHz itself or leave it alone.

source.quote: Shanling's own manual for the EH90, EH90v1.0.pdf, read 2026-11-25. The product page /product/495 is 16 image slices, and the announcement /article/101202 carries no specification list at all - it says only « Visit the dedicated product page of EH90 to view all the details: LINK », which is the images. So the manual is the only text source. Rear panel, verbatim: « 1. Bluetooth Antenna / 2. WORD/CLK Input / 3. Digital AES/EBU Input / 4. Digital Coaxial Input / 5. Digital Optical Input / 6. USB Input / 7. Digital IIS-LVDS Input / 8. Digital HDMI-ARC Input / 9. Power Switch / 10. Power Connector / 11. RCA Analog Output / 12. Balanced Analog Output ». « Input Options / Press the [ / MENU ] wheel to access Input settings or press the [SOURCE] button to cycle between inputs: "BT / COAXIAL / OPTICAL / AES EBU / USB / I2S / HDMI-ARC" ». « Tone Filter / Available in settings, switch between OS (Oversampling) and NOS (Non-oversampling) data processing of DAC. Oversampling filter will process all audio at 352.8kHz. » Its sampling-frequency indicator table reads « 32/44.1/48kHz - Blue »; « 64/88.2/96kHz - Green »; « 128/176.4/192kHz - Yellow »; « 352.8/384/705.6/768kHz - Purple »; « DSD64/128/256/512 - White ». Settings menu: « Language / Gain / Tone Filter / Clock Input / IIS Input mode / Screen brightness / Screen-Off time / Light switch / Reset Settings / About ». The manual prints full IIS-LVDS pinout tables for several pin modes. From the announcement: « The high-end Shanling PRO R2R module was firstly introduced in our flagship SCD3.3 SACD player, later also adapted into the SM1.3R Streamer. »; « offering up to 5.2W @ 32Ohm »; « Launching this month and available at 1199 USD // 1299 Euro. » No « support up to » figure is declared anywhere, and no converter part number is given.

data.chip: « AKM AK4493 DAC » with a « 3rd Generation FPGA » and « OPA2211 as low pass filter » - and the maker's own correction attached: « Due to printing error, some units of EM5 show OPA1612 in their diagram. Actual component used is OPA2211 ».

device_settings.why: « CPAF Filter technology » is named and nothing more: no count, no list, no explanation of what CPAF stands for. Named-but-opaque, which is a third shape beside the makers who give a count without names and those who give neither.

data.chip: « 使用一片罗姆BD34302EKV解码芯片 » - one ROHM BD34302EKV. USB receiver « XMOS XU-316 », clock circuit « CK-03 » (the product page renders it « CK-O3 » with a letter O). External 10 MHz or atomic clock input supported, but there is no built-in OCXO row as on the two larger models.

device_settings.why: Two named positions, « SHARP ROLL-OFF » and « SLOW ROLL-OFF », as on its siblings.

THREE positions where the D3R and D2R MK2 have six, and named only in Chinese as low, mid and high cut-off - no kHz figure for any of them. So the same menu is both shorter and less specified on the cheaper model, which is a difference between products rather than a gap in the document.
« NORMAL (普通，PS AUDIO格式) » and « REVERSED (反转，DATA和LRCK反转) » - named differently from the D3R's and D2R MK2's « MODE1(PS Audio) / MODE2 », and more informatively: this one says what is reversed.

source.quote: SMSL's own MANUAL for the VMV D1R, VMVD1RManual.pdf, read 2026-11-25 - the document that carries the per-socket table. Its product page at https://www.smsl-audio.com/portal/product/detail/id/964.html is quoted alongside for the Introduction text and carries NO specification table of its own.  Introduction tab, verbatim with the maker's own typos and missing spaces: « High sound quality design, using a ROHM BD34302EKV decoding chip,THD+N as low as 0.00017%(-115 dB); »; « USB, optical and coaxial all support MQA decoding function and MQA-CD;USB and iPs support Native DSD input, and coaxial and optical supportDOP64; »; « XMOS XU-316,32-bit USB solution, supports DoP and native DSD, PCMsupports up to 768kHz, and DSD supports DSD512; »; « The self-developed CK-O3 clock processing circuit greatly reduces the clockjitter; »; « Support external clock input, standard 10MHz clock or atomic clock input; » - « iPs » is the site's rendering of I2S and « CK-O3 » uses a letter O where the manual prints CK-03. The manual's Chinese feature lines: « 高音质设计，使用一片罗姆BD34302EKV解码芯片，失真度低至0.00017%（-115dB)；»; « USB、光纤、同轴均支持 MQA 解码功能, 并且支持MQA-CD；»; « USB、I2S支持DSD输入，同轴、光纤支持DOP64；» The manual's Chinese specification table (技术参数), verbatim: « 输入方式 USB/光纤/同轴/I2S/蓝牙 »; « MQA解码 USB / 光纤 / 同轴 »; for « USB/I2S »: « PCM 44.1~768kHz(32bit) », « DSD 2.8224~22.5792MHz(1bit) »; for « USB »: « DoP 2.8224~11.2896MHz(1bit) »; for « 光纤/同轴 »: « PCM 44.1~192kHz(24bit) », « DoP 2.8224MHz(1bit) ». Device-level: « 动态范围 124dB / 123dB »; « 消耗功率 <15W »; « 待机功耗 <0.5W »; « 重量 1.48kg/3.26lbs ». The INPUTS menu: « USB », « BLUETOOTH », « OPTICAL », « COAXIAL », « I2S(HDMI) » - there is NO AES/EBU on this model, and the input list and the MQA row both stop at USB, optical, coaxial, I2S and Bluetooth. The manual's PCM FILTER menu: « SHARP ROLL-OFF (快速滚降) » and « SLOW ROLL-OFF （慢速滚降) ». Its DSD FILTER menu: « 低截止频率 », « 中截止频率 », « 高截止频率 » - THREE positions, printed in Chinese only, as low, mid and high cut-off frequency, with NO English labels and NO kHz figures. The six-value 26k to 157k list of the bigger models is absent here. The product page carries NO specification table in text - its tabs are only Introduction, Colour, Download and Purchase Link, and the lower half is marketing JPEGs, from which no figure was read.

data.chip: ROHM BD34302EKV converting, XMOS XU-316 as the USB interface. Note the part number against smsl/d200's BD34352EKV: two ROHM parts, one family, two models.

device_settings.set_to: SLOW ROLL-OFF (the maker's own « best sound » preset)
device_settings.why: Two named positions, « SHARP ROLL-OFF » and « SLOW ROLL-OFF », AND the manual prints what each of its two one-button presets sets them to: « DEFAULT： PCM FILTER: SHARP ROLL-OFF / DSD FILTER: 26kHz CUT-OFF » and « BEST SOUND： PCM FILTER: SLOW ROLL-OFF / DSD FILTER: 157kHz CUT-OFF ». A maker stating which of its own filter positions it considers best is unique in this catalogue - nine makers have published a count and withheld the names, and this one publishes the names AND its own preference.

device_settings.set_to: 157kHz CUT-OFF (the maker's own « best sound » preset)
device_settings.why: Six positions named by cut-off frequency, and the « BEST SOUND » preset selects the highest of them, 157 kHz - the least filtering. The « DEFAULT » preset selects the lowest, 26 kHz. So the maker ships the device filtered and offers a button that unfilters it.
« MODE1(PS Audio) » and « MODE2 », as on the D3R.

data.chip: ROHM BD34302EKV - the same part as smsl/vmv-d2r-mk2 - with an XMOS XU-316 as the USB interface.

device_settings.why: Two positions, both NAMED: « SHARP ROLL-OFF (快速滚降) » and « SLOW ROLL-OFF （慢速滚降) ». This is the ROHM filter set, not the ESS seven-filter list - no ESS filter name appears anywhere in the VMV range. Two named positions is the shortest complete filter list in the catalogue, and completeness is what matters: a reader can act on it.

SIX positions, each named by its cut-off frequency: 26k, 39k, 52k, 78k, 104k, 157k. A DSD reconstruction filter is analogue and sets how much of the format's own out-of-band noise reaches the output - so this is not an interpolation filter and choosing among them does not touch `correctable`. Recorded because six published cut-off frequencies for DSD is unique in the catalogue.

« MODE1(PS Audio) (模式1（PS Audio)) » and « MODE2 (模式2) », with the maker's own note « 注: 这个选项用于匹配不同的I2S接口标准, 使用前请检查信号源的接口定义。» - the option exists because I2S over HDMI has no single pin standard, and the owner must check the source's pinout. There is also « I2S DSD CHANNEL » with « DSDL=PCM DATA » and « DSDL=PCM LRCK », which swaps the DSD channels on that input only.

source.quote: Soekris Engineering's own page for the dac1221, read 2026-11-25. Self-description: « Entry Level Discrete R-2R Sign Magnitude DAC ». On the ladder: « It have the fantastic clean and natural sound of a 26 bit R-2R sign magnitude DAC, built with two hundred tiny and very precise thin film resistors ». « Resistor Precision 26 bit, 0.02% - 0.05% Resistors ». Inputs: « SPDIF / Toslink Inputs Up to 24 bit / 192 Khz »; « USB Input PCM Up to 24 Bit / 384 Ksps »; « USB Input DSD Up to DoP-128 and DSD-256 ». Filters: « with a set of selectable advanced digital filters and a digital volume control. » Measurement: « THD @ -1 dB <0.008% ». The word NOS appears nowhere on the page, and there is no AES/EBU input.

source.quote: Soulution's own page for the 560, read 2026-11-24. Table headed « Bit depth/sampling rage max » (the misspelling is the page's): « AES/EBU: 24 bit/192 kHz »; « SPDIF: 24 bit/192 kHz »; « Optical: 24 bit/96 kHz »; « USB: 24 bit/384 kHz, 1 bit/5.64 MHz »; « Network: 24 bit/384 kHz, 1 bit/5.64 MHz ». Digital inputs listed as « AES/EBU, SPDIF-RCA, Optical, USB, Network ». On the conversion stage: « Burr-Brown devices perform D/A conversion only. Their internal upsampling and filter stages are not used. » and « Our players and D/A converters use an algorithm from the highly regarded Anagram Technologies followed by Burr Brown D/A converters in a digital symmetric configuration. » On the signal path: « Audio data is buffered then upsampled to 24Bit/384kHz. » On the analogue stage: « The 560's 3rd order bessel filter, with a cut-off frequency of 120kHz, does show a phase shift of up to 15 degrees in the audio band. » and « Due to the Zero-Phase-Technology the phase error of the analog music signal remains below 1 degree, 20Hz - 100kHz! ». Self-description: « soulution 560 D/A converter » and « The 560 D/A-Converter does excell at exactly this task. It captures all digital music data and transports it in the analog domain. »

open_doubt.text: Whether this device reconverts DSD to PCM. The temptation is strong and the page does not close it. « Audio data is buffered then upsampled to 24Bit/384kHz » describes the signal path with no exception; the inputs accept « 1 bit/5.64 MHz »; the output of that stage is stated as 24-bit PCM. Read together they say DSD arrives, meets a PCM upsampler and leaves as 24/384 - which would make dsd_reconverted_to_pcm true. But « Audio data » is the maker's word for everything it had been talking about, which was PCM, and the sentence never says the 1-bit stream takes that path. No fact is written. Getting this field wrong is expensive: it is what tells an engine whether sending DSD to this device is worth anything at all, and the cascade carries it almost everywhere: re-measured 2026-11-24, 56 of the 59 records that resolve it at all take it from their family, 3 from evidence of their own.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: One sentence from Soulution about what happens to a 1-bit input, or a manual. Failing that, a measurement: feed DSD128 and look for the PCM signature. Do NOT resolve it by reading the upsampling sentence harder.

data.chip: « der AKM AK4493 SEQ VELVETSOUND » (Asahi Kasei), inside a module SPL calls the « DAC768v2 ». The « 120V-Technologie » working at « +/-60 V » and the « SLP120 (Super Low-Pass) » filter are the ANALOGUE output stage and its reconstruction filter - SPL's whole selling point, and not the converter.

source.quote: SPL's own page for the Phonitor 3 DAC, read 2026-11-25. The page is German-only. On USB: « Ueber USB wandelt der Phonitor 3 DAC PCM-Audio-Signale mit einer Aufloesung von 32 Bit und einer Abtastrate von bis zu 768 kHz sowie DSD-Signale mit einer Aufloesung von bis zu DSD256. » On the S/PDIF coaxial and optical inputs and on AES/EBU, each described in its own sentence: « mit Abtastraten von bis zu 192 kHz und einer Wortbreite von 16 Bit bis 24 Bit empfangen » and, for AES/EBU, « maximalen Abtastrate von 192 kHz und einer Wortbreite von 16 Bit bis 24 Bit ». On the converter: « Als Wandler-Chip im Digital/Analog-Wandler des Phonitor 3 DAC kommt ... der DAC768v2 ... der AKM AK4493 SEQ VELVETSOUND(TM) ». On DSD in the DAC768v2 section: « Auch Direct Stream Digital wird bis zu einer Aufloesung von DSD4 bzw. DSD256 unterstuetzt. » On the analogue stage: « Die 120V-Technologie arbeitet mit +/-60 V » and an analogue reconstruction filter « SLP120 (Super Low-Pass) », « ein analogen 'Super Low-Pass'-Filter mit 120V-Technologie ». spl.audio has no prohibition: the Impressum and the AGB were both READ and neither restricts copying, reproduction or extraction; the only rights line is the footer « (c) 2026 SPL electronics GmbH ».

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.
data.chip: The maker's own discrete DSD stage, with no DSP in the DSD path. Not a commercial converter chip, and a case where an architecture family fits without inventing anything.

device_settings.why: « UAC 1.0 / 2.0 (switchable) », and the input table rates the two as SEPARATE INTERFACES: UAC 2.0 takes 44.1-384 kHz and DSD, UAC 1.0 takes 44.1-48 kHz and no DSD at all. A factor of EIGHT on the rate, decided by a menu setting. UAC 1.0 exists for hosts with no driver; anything this engine runs on supports 2.0.

device_settings.set_to: F-8: Minimum Phase Slow Roll-Off Low Dispersion
device_settings.why: Eight filters, all named. F-8 is chosen: minimum phase has no pre-ringing, and the maker marks this one low-dispersion, which is the cost minimum phase otherwise pays. F-5 is the factory default and is linear phase, so leaving the device alone leaves pre-ringing in the path. Note F-2, « Linear Phase Fast Roll-Off Apodizing » - the third apodising filter found in this catalogue and the first offered as one of eight.

data.chip: Not named anywhere in the manual.

device_settings.why: Six named filters. F-6 is chosen: short delay is this maker's word for the minimum-phase family, which has no pre-ringing, and F-6 is the low-dispersion variant of it. F-3, the factory default, is also short delay but without the low-dispersion correction.

Two DSD filters, given as cut-off frequencies: « F-1 + DSD: 37kHz (Default) » and « F-2 + DSD: 65kHz ». The wider one is preferred for the same reason RME's « Wild Bandwidth » setting is preferred elsewhere in this catalogue: a DSD stream's noise is out of band, and a filter that cuts at 37 kHz is removing signal as well. BUT SEE THE CONSTRAINT BELOW - this setting is not always available.

« m-p: Preamp mode (volume adjustable) (Default) » against « m-d: DAC mode (volume not adjustable) ». DAC mode takes the volume control out of the path entirely, which is what you want when the device feeds an amplifier that has its own. First record in the catalogue where a setting removes the attenuator rather than improving it.

Section « 10. Input range »: « USB IN | PCM 44.1kHz-768kHz/16bit-32bit | DSD DSD64-DSD512 (Native), DSD64-DSD256 (Dop) | PEQ 44.1kHz-192kHz/16bit-32bit »; « OPT/COAX IN (S/PDIF) | PCM 44.1kHz-192kHz/16bit-24bit | DSD DSD64 (Dop) | PEQ 44.1kHz-192kHz/16bit-24bit »; « OPT IN (ADAT) | PCM 44.1kHz-192kHz | PEQ 44.1kHz-192kHz »; « BT IN | AAC/SBC/APTX/APTX-Adaptive/APTX HD/LDAC | PEQ 44.1kHz-96kHz/16bit-24bit ». Section « 9. Attribute »: « Signal input USB/OPT/COAX/BT »; « Measured 15.5cm x 12.9cm x 4.1cm ». Rear panel: « 6. Optical input (Supports and automatically recognizes S/PDIF and ADAT protocols) ». On ADAT: « E50 II automatically detects S/PDIF and ADAT protocols from the optical input, with no manual switching required »; « Supports 44.1-192 kHz sample rates with automatic detection, no setup »; and a table « Relationship between ADAT sampling rate mode and ADAT input channel » giving « AdA1 » four channel pairs (1-2, 3-4, 5-6, 7-8), « AdA2 » two pairs, « AdA4 » one pair. PCM filter: « F-1 + PCM: Sharp Roll-off Filter »; « F-2 + PCM: Slow Roll-off Filter »; « F-3 + PCM: Short Delay Sharp Roll-off Filter (Default) »; « F-4 + PCM: Short Delay Slow Roll-off Filter »; « F-5 + PCM: Super Slow Roll-off Filter »; « F-6 + PCM: Low-dispersion Short Delay Filter ». DSD filter: « F-1 + DSD: 37kHz (Default) »; « F-2 + DSD: 65kHz », with the note « When the output amplitude is in high voltage mode, the DSD filter is fixed at F-1 and cannot be adjusted. » Decoding mode: « m-p: Preamp mode (volume adjustable) (Default) »; « m-d: DAC mode (volume not adjustable) ». Output amplitude: « U-L: Low (Default) »; « U-H: High ». The manual names no DAC chip. toppingaudio.com has no terms-of-use page at all.

data.chip: No converter chip: « R2R DAC technology using 600 pieces of 0.01% VAR Bulk Metal Foil resistors Vishay Foil Resistors », « the famous naked Vishay foil ». The maker counts its resistors and names their tolerance and their supplier, which is more than any chip datasheet in this catalogue says about its own silicon - and still gives no ladder bit depth, the field that is known for 7 records of 61.

device_settings.name: Non-oversampling DAC compensation filter
device_settings.why_it_matters: A filter the listener can switch off. Second such setting in this catalogue after RME's five DA filters, and the second argument that internal_bypass - which assumes a RATE threshold - is modelled for the rarer shape.

open_doubt.text: KEPT ON PURPOSE, against the move that took its two neighbours out. This record shares their identity - brand "unknown", model "unknown" - and it is not the same kind of thing. Its source says so: « Not a device. The record the engine uses when the driver reports an identity no record matches and the listener has not said. » It is the TERMINAL of the cascade, the bottom a consumer resolves to when nothing else matches, and deleting it would remove the floor rather than a duplicate. akm-generique and ess-generique were chip defaults wearing a device; this one is the absence of a device, which is a role no chip family can fill.
open_doubt.what_is_doubtful: Its `kind` says "dac", which is the one field that is plainly wrong: it is not a converter, it is the answer "we do not know which converter". And it carries dsd_direct false where its chip family says "unknown" - both end in the conservative branch, so nothing breaks, but two levels still disagree. The real question is whether a terminal belongs in devices/ at all, or whether a consumer should get it from the vocabulary instead of from a record that has to pretend to be a device to exist.

data.chip: No part number, and the maker goes out of its way not to give one: « a chosen DAC chip », corrected from outside by a « Dual-differential musIC 3 128-bit-feed-forward error correction process », with « Processing is done at 128 bit internal resolution ». So bought silicon, deliberately unnamed, with the maker's own correction ahead of it.

source.quote: Wadax's own page for the Atlantis Reference DAC, read 2026-11-24. Specification block, « Inputs: »: « USB (32-384KHz, 16-24-32 bits, DSD64, DSD128, DSD256, MQA) »; « 2xSPDIF RCA (32KHz-192KHz, 16-24 bits) »; « 2xSPDIF BNC (32KHz-192KHz, 16-24 bits) »; « 2xAES-EBU (32KHz-192KHz, 16-24 bits) »; « Native Reference Wadax Link (native PCM, DSD), 3xAES-EBU, 1 RJ45 »; « Optional: WADAX Akasa Optical Module ». On the processing: « By mapping the error mechanisms of a chosen DAC chip under load using Adaptive Delta Hilbert Mapping »; « Dual-differential musIC 3 128-bit-feed-forward error correction process »; « Processing is done at 128 bit internal resolution »; « Zepto Reference clock: doubled the master clock frequency with only 12fs total jitter. »; « including native DSD replay over our proprietary triple AES-EBU connection ». Self-description: « The Atlantis REFERENCE DAC is our response to these findings, with lower levels of clock noise and significant improvements in PSU and mechanical isolation. » and « The result is the most accurate and most musically satisfying DAC ever designed. » The page also carries spec images at images/dacConnectivity.png and images/dacInNumbers.png, not opened: the text above is the page's own.

data.chip: ES9028PRO (ESS) - but SCOPED TO AN EDITION, in the maker's own words: « The MK2 version features a newly upgraded DAC board with an ES9028PRO chip ». The page says nothing about what the pre-MK2 DAC204 used, so this chip is a fact about the MK2 and not about every unit sold under the name.

source.quote: Weiss Engineering's own page for the DAC204-MK2, read 2026-11-24. « Digital Inputs The DAC204 has a total of three digital stereo inputs: USB Two AES/EBU or S/PDIF on Toslink or RCA connectors. open_doubt.text:
TWO DOUBTS, AND THE FIRST IS THE MOST VALUABLE QUESTION IN THIS CATALOGUE.
1. Weiss writes « The unit can also convert DSD audio to PCM and offers a digital output in AES/EBU format. » If that means DSD is re-converted internally before analogue conversion, dsd_reconverted_to_pcm is true and a consumer should never send this device DSD. If it means the unit can transcode DSD to PCM for its AES/EBU digital output, the field is untouched. The sentence supports both readings. One email to Weiss settles it - which is exactly the inlet this catalogue rates highest and has never used.
2. The ES9028PRO is stated for « the MK2 version » only. By this catalogue's own rule an edition becomes a record of its own the day a fact distinguishes it, and a different converter board is such a fact. So DAC204-MK2 has earned a record - the first alias typed `edition` to do so - and what the pre-MK2 used is unknown. Nine households own a « DAC204 » with no generation stated.

device_settings.why: « selectable PCM/DSD filters » - the maker says they are selectable, names none and counts none. This is one of only TWO filter mentions in xDuoo's entire catalogue, the other being the Link2 Max's « five filters ». Eleventh maker in four days to publish the existence of a filter menu and withhold its contents.
